_doc: Virgil Haught, Haught and Son funeral home. He and his father prepared the Silver Bridge dead in December 1967. The hub's shows table answers Ada's carl_last_words. Topics on the hub offer his quick facts (antifreeze, two of the forty-six).

open.speaker: undertaker
lines: Haught and Son. I'm the son. Father's been in the back room since '81, in the sense that matters.
If you've come about the dog, the county has it. If you've come about the bridge, the county has nothing, and neither do I.
Sit if you like. The chairs are for the bereaved, but nobody's booked till Thursday.
The building's full. He knows it. He's been polite to them for thirty years.

passives.line: Thermostat reads seventy. Two sweaters on the man. He keeps the room warm for a reason that isn't comfort.
'In the sense that matters.' An undertaker who talks like that has kept a ledger of more than names.

static.line: Forty-six. He counted them in here. Two of them are still counting.

options.text: We're sorry to come in on a working day, Mr. Haught.
Eighteen degrees under the air, two hours after. Antifreeze doesn't do that. What does?
Your father taught you the trade. Did he teach you what to do when the trade doesn't work?
(Sit in the chairs for the bereaved. Say nothing.)

working.speaker: undertaker
lines: Every day's a working day. Winter's the busy season, on a hill of old people with coal furnaces.
You're courteous. That's rarer than you'd think in your line. Ask.

cold_dog.speaker: undertaker
lines: ...Nothing I can write on a county form.
I've seen it twice before, and neither was a dog, and the room was seventy then too. Save your film. I mean that kindly now.

cold_dog_fail.speaker: undertaker
lines: Antifreeze, sir. I said it to the deputy and I'll say it to you. Dogs lie down in the snow and the snow does the rest.
Walt Jessup up the road has lost animals too. Go and tell him it's a mystery. See how far you get.

father.speaker: undertaker
lines: He taught me to write it in the margin and say nothing. He wrote in the margins. I write in the margins.
It's what we have instead of church. The ledger's in the back. I don't show it. I'm telling you it exists. The county never got that.
Margins. That's where this whole town keeps the truth.

father_fail.speaker: undertaker
lines: My father is not a subject. He's a name on the window.
Opal Fry keeps the obituaries at the library. She'll tell you what's public. I'll tell you what's for sale, which is caskets.

sit.speaker: undertaker
lines: You sit like people who've buried someone. Hands in your lap. All right.
Ask. I'll say what I can say in this room.

hub.speaker: undertaker
hub.prompt: The bereaved get an hour. I'll give you the same.
lines: The bereaved get an hour. I'll give you the same.

options.text: The drawing in the margin. You drew it the week before. You saw it on the bridge before it fell.
Seventy on the dial and two sweaters. Who's the heat for?
We'll leave you to your families, Mr. Haught.

drawing.speaker: undertaker
lines: ...Thursday the fourteenth. I was on the Ohio side for a casket spray. It was on the top chord, standing the way a man stands on a ladder.
Looking down the deck at the cars. Not at me. At the cars, one after another, like it was reading the plates.
I drew it that night. I did not tell Carl Mercer, who took tolls. I had a whole week and I did not tell him. Write that in your margin.
They don't blame you, Virgil. I'd tell you if they did.

drawing_fail.speaker: undertaker
lines: Those margins are between me and my father, and he's in the back room.
The side door, please. The front is for families.

carl.speaker: undertaker
lines: Ada told you. Then she told you about the light. I'll give you the part she doesn't have.
Carl came in here on the twelfth, in his toll coat, and asked what it cost to be buried without water in you. I thought he was drinking.
He wasn't drinking. He'd seen it sing. Three notes, he said, and tapped them on my desk. I've never told her that. Don't you.
He's in the grey chair, Virgil. He's not angry either.

heat.speaker: undertaker
lines: The room. I keep the room at seventy. Since '67.
If something comes in cold I want to know by morning whether it's warming. Mostly they do. Mostly.
